**Seed revision, 18 October 2026:** The current request supersedes the earlier open-license-only sourcing criterion. Seed cases use the frozen public-page package with 100 movies, 100 TV series and 200 matched posters, attributed source links and supplied rights information; no provider API/account or startup network fetch is required. Focused verification consists of one package validation, a small invalid-input/retry/preservation/recovery regression set, one fresh installation and one upgrade smoke, a batch poster response check, and one movie/TV detail inspection. Existing broader release cases remain unexecuted unless separately evidenced; this change does not claim a full acceptance sweep.

---

## Authority, actors and scope

SpoolIn lets readers discover movies, TV series and the people behind them. Maintainers manage movies and shared people, credits and artwork, and may approve an exact new-movie proposal in ChatGPT or Claude. A fresh installation starts with exactly 100 distinct movies and 100 distinct TV series. That count is an initial seed obligation, not a later cap or reset instruction.

The current user invocation governs this phase. [PRD v2.4](02-PRD.md) owns product behavior. The [adopted design system](design-system/index.md) owns presentation and interaction. [Techdoc v1.10](04-spoolin-techdoc.md) and its [approved invocation constraints](prompts/techdoc-creation.md) own selected engineering within those commitments. [Brainstorming](01-brainstorming-result.md) records history: earlier open/recommended roles, registration exclusions, database, retry defaults and standalone seed commands do not reopen later accepted decisions. Mockup values, timers and slash-separated credit fields are examples, not server rules. In particular, character strings are arrays of complete names; a slash inside one name survives.

Carry forward TD-U-001–007: PostgreSQL/JPA; one-command initialization; separate top-level TypeScript MCP adapter; local application with Claude Desktop stdio and ChatGPT private outbound tunnel; exactly one notification mode with **database recording by default**; openly reusable frozen seed facts; shared database contracts. TD-U-005 supersedes the older external-delivery-only interpretation of FR-015, AC-061/062/063/082 and brainstorming D21. Database mode proves durable RECORDED status; external acceptance/delivery claims require real selected-provider evidence. Techdoc retry defaults are three **total** attempts, 500 ms base, factor 2 and 5, 000 ms cap; older four-attempt proposals are superseded. Selected text/file defaults now come from techdoc §11.1, including adopted PRD recommendations. Full application hosting remains deferred; private MCP connectivity is required.

| Actor | Acceptance boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Visitor | Public active catalog/people/credits, registration and sign-in |
| Viewer | Same public reading plus own authenticated session; no catalog management, archive or audit |
| Maintainer A / B | Same management powers; owned draft/operation/cancel and connector isolation still apply |
| Connected assistant | Limited new-movie context/proposal/status; no independent approval, editing/deletion, account, archive, audit or artwork authority |
| Local operator / reviewer / developer | Installation and evidence responsibilities; no additional browser role or implied application privilege |
| Core / Catalog / Media / MCP principal | Verified service identity with method allowlist and scoped human context where required |

### Permission decision table (F-PERMISSIONS)

Use this table for every operation boundary, including direct attempts hidden by the UI. Contribution labels Actor/Director/Writer/Producer and Cast/Creator never grant account permissions.

| Capability | Visitor | Viewer | Maintainer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active public titles/people/credits/search/filters | Allow | Allow | Allow with public predicates |
| Register / sign in | Allow anonymous registration/sign-in | Use assigned account; sign-out available | Use assigned account; sign-out available |
| Movie/person/role/credit/artwork management | Deny | Deny | Allow only valid active-record operations |
| Private movie/people archive, restore/delete | Deny | Deny | Allow archive-first/current version/current confirmation |
| Read-only catalog audit | Deny | Deny | Allow sanitized history |
| Own recoverable permitted draft / receipt | Anonymous registration scope only where defined | Own eligible data only | Own eligible data only |
| Exact AI publication | Deny | Deny | Trusted human review, current connector/permission/policy and exact revision only |
| Direct TV editing, TV artwork/credits/lifecycle; account role selection/directory | Deny | Deny | Deny |

Shared-person changes may indirectly change displayed seeded TV credits while TV titles remain active/read-only. Public credit visibility always requires both active title and active person. Restoring either record does not restore the other or recreate deleted records/removed credits. Audit supports accountability without exposing account email/credentials or enabling arbitrary restoration.

Ratings/reviews, critic aggregation, journaling, tracking, community and season/episode entities are deferred. Email verification/recovery, role/account administration, in-app AI approval queues and configuration screens are excluded. Those excluded capabilities have no artificial successful-action cases; their denial/no-control boundaries remain covered where applicable.

## Approach and fixtures

P0 covers severe authorization, privacy, loss, duplicate-effect and irreversible-lifecycle risks. P1 covers committed functionality, contracts, operations and recovery; no committed obligation is omitted for lower priority. **Level** names the primary proof boundary; **Platform** names the surface; **Category** is Positive/Negative/Edge; **Automation** says Candidate/Manual; **Status** is execution evidence. A candidate is prospective, not implemented automation. Unit/component checks may isolate rules and faults, but contracts, PostgreSQL transactions, network cancellation, filesystem durability, provider delivery and actual client behavior need the named real boundary.

A case with several table or recipe rows requires independently reset setup and separately recorded results for every row. Use equivalence classes, inclusive limit − 1 / limit / limit + 1, role/visibility matrices, state transitions and coordinated fault timelines. Shared scenarios do not authorize run-order dependence. Expected IDs and protected side effects are hand-checked from fixtures, never calculated by copying implementation logic. Each Then is the oracle; Verification states how to observe it and what boundary a double cannot prove. Rejecting a write requires both the correct safe failure and the absence of prohibited partial effects.

| Coverage family | Required boundary / selection |
| --- | --- |
| Product/UI | Discovery, accounts, movie/person/credit/artwork/archive/audit, every inventoried UI state, both themes and responsive/accessibility contracts |
| Contracts | Browser HTTP/GraphQL, generated `spoolin.v1` gRPC, MCP input/output/resource and selected provider; allow/deny/presence/precision/errors/deadline/cancel |
| Data integrity | Every inventoried column/DDL constraint, owner transaction/audit/work, concurrent versions/impact, native mappings/plans, seed and migration preservation |
| Reliability | Repeated intent versus similar data, request binding, lost replies, durable attempts/leases/crashes, cancellation, exhaustion and controlled recovery |
| Security/privacy | Sessions/CSRF/service assertions, own data, plain-text/injection/file bounds, cryptographic nonce/rotation/restore, redaction and least privilege |
| Operations/performance | Seven Make commands and operator tools, dependency readiness/exits, test isolation, shutdown, backpressure, metrics/alerts, protected backup/restore; approved local workload and actual evidence boundaries |
| MCP/providers | Independent real ChatGPT and Claude evidence, trustworthy exact approval, host refusal, provenance/private-data restrictions; simulation and provider receipts labeled |
| Coverage integrity | Independently inventoried sources, reciprocal references, explicit gaps/exclusions, stable/retired IDs and fresh evidence |

### C-RESET: shared cleanup

Preserve sanitized per-row receipt/state/evidence, reset the case’s fixtures, clock and fault barriers; revoke only its synthetic sessions/connectors and release browser/file/process handles. Remove only its unique disposable namespace/volumes and restore changed test configuration. Normal application data, real provider destinations and shared client credentials remain outside cleanup. Document-only reviews require no runtime cleanup. Each case invokes this same explicit reset contract independently.

### F-STACK: isolated future runtime

Create a uniquely named disposable installation `atdd-<run UUID>` with PostgreSQL 18.6 service-owned `spoolin_core`, `spoolin_catalog`, `spoolin_media` databases, separate runtime/migrator/maintenance test roles, real Core/Catalog/Media TCP gRPC and bounded private Media volume. Build the selected Kotlin/Spring and Svelte/TypeScript/Node stack from locked images/dependencies. Use independently provisioned synthetic keys/certificates and loopback test ports; no normal database, volume, credentials or client connector may be reused. Keep each row’s baseline snapshot and fault barrier separate. This fixture does not exist yet; its implementation belongs to the next phase.

### F-ACTORS: independent identities

Provision Viewer V and Maintainers A/B with independent UUIDs, sessions and auth epochs. Registration fixtures use synthetic `a@example.test`, `b@example.test` identities and permitted names. Supply invented exact passwords through protected test input, never this document’s execution artifacts or recovery drafts. A/B have equal catalog powers; B cannot retrieve A’s draft, private operation or upload cancellation. Create distinct service certificates for SAN `core`, `catalog`, `media`, `mcp`, and separate CLAUDE/CHATGPT connector grants bound to A. Invalid/expired/revoked/wrong-role identities are independently configured rows.

### F-CATALOG and F-ORDER: deterministic metadata

Use a fixed test namespace UUID `c1bb0e81-232b-5f83-9d73-a5273dcac001`; derive fixture IDs with UUIDv5(namespace, the literal label below). Record the derived values in the run fixture before execution. Source-qualified identities are `fixture/<label>`, never title/name matching. Ordinary versions start at 5. Set title creation instants to 2026-10-12T03:00:00Z so release filtering cannot accidentally use createdAt.

| Label | Starting values |
| --- | --- |
| M-A | MOVIE, ACTIVE, The Last Light, original Cahaya, synopsis “A pilot returns home.”, G-Drama + G-Mystery, release 2024-10-09, optional runtime108, OLD attachment |
| M-B | MOVIE, ACTIVE unless row archives it, same display title, G-Documentary, release 2024 year-only, no optional facts; may share OLD through a separate hold |
| TV-C | TV, ACTIVE, Letters from Tomorrow, G-Drama, first-air2024-10, CONTINUING, unknown end and episode runtime |
| U-D | MOVIE, ACTIVE, Unknown Horizon, G-Drama, unknown release components, no artwork; imported read fixture, never invalid manual create |
| M-D | MOVIE, ACTIVE, A Map of Quiet Places, G-Documentary, 2023-03; additional impact target |
| P-A / P-B / P-C | Shared people Alex / Alex / V; P-A ACTIVE, P-B ARCHIVED, P-C ACTIVE; names do not merge IDs |
| Credits | P-A Actor and Director on M-A, Writer on M-B and Actor onTV-C; P-B retained Actor onM-A; each row establishes/removes its own relationships |
| Starter roles | CAST Actor allows characters; CREATOR Director/Writer/Producer; custom roles default characters=false |
| F-ORDER additions | Same-year full date/month-only/year-only, older year, unknown date and equal-date UUID ties; mixed-case/Unicode and duplicate display titles; creation instants independent of release dates with microsecond and UUID ties. Exercise all six orders; default year/month/day DESC NULLS LAST, UUID ASC. |

F-FILTER is the M-A/M-B/TV-C/U-D subset of F-CATALOG. Hand-check filter oracles: with M-A/M-B/TV-C/U-D baseline, year 2024 returns M-A, M-B, TV-C; October2024 returns M-A, TV-C; MOVIE+Drama+October2024 returns M-A. Genre selections use OR and separate categories use AND. Same-name records remain independent. Public P-B credits never appear; F-LIFECYCLE uses the lifecycle truth table: both ACTIVE→visible, any archived endpoint→private. Unknown optional context never becomes zero, fabricated January1 or guessed artwork.

### F-CLOCK, F-WORK and fault timeline

Control the observation clock at 2026-10-12T03:00:00Z and move it explicitly relative to source deadlines/retention. Use deterministic jitter draws 0, middle and upper allowed bound in rule checks; record actual random sampling in integration. Production cryptographic randomness must remain secure and is never replaced by deterministic fixture tokens. Synchronize W1/W2 and concurrent sessions with barriers at before local commit, after commit/before reply, before remote send, after remote commit/before receipt, after lease loss and before cleanup unlink. Never use elapsed sleeps as the only completion proof. F-EXPIRY specifies exact equality; logical expiry is independent of physical purge.

F-WORK starts from parent operation O and deterministic child UUIDv5(parent, stable step name), generation 0, explicit max attempts, nextAttemptAt and deadlineAt. Configure READY/LEASED/DONE/EXHAUSTED/CANCELLED independently. Reconciliation sees the destination’s real receipt, not a mock call count. Restart cannot change the saved budget. Recovery reasons and operator identities are synthetic and sanitized.

### F-ART and F-IMAGES: bounded independent files

OLD/NEW are different static licensed or generated test images with independently measured SHA-256, dimensions, format and byte count. Supply valid staticJPEG/PNG/WebP;0-byte, random1-byte, exact5, 242, 880 and one-above files; malformed/disguised/animatedAPNG/WebP/GIF/SVG/polyglot fixtures; dimension8191/8192/8193, pixel39, 999, 999/40, 000, 000/40, 000, 001 and resource-bound examples. A size-exact supported file may use a valid independently verified bounded ancillary segment; it still must fully decode and satisfy every other limit. Separate byte acceptance from content acceptance. Source limits independently cap decoded160Mbytes, RSS256 MiB, CPU5 s, wall10 s, temp32 MiB, output8 MiB. Never use real private user files. Reserve/attach/cancel/cleanup cases record immutable asset/hold/title/operation tuples and actual selected bytes before/after.

### F-BROWSER-POLICY: scoped future browser security evidence

Use the [production storage/restore policy](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#341-browser-storage-and-restored-page-state) and [cookie lifecycle](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#851-cookie-lifecycle-contract) through a unique disposable production browser origin/profile and real trusted HTTPS/Core. Keep synthetic A/B and storage/cookie canaries isolated; record only redacted attributes, classifications, booleans and permitted IDs. Observe application calls before startup plus intermediate/final browser stores; a clean store alone is no absence proof. Cookie capture is privileged transient test-driver memory, never an application store or raw report/HAR. Test frontend and served review code, keeping real chat-host isolation as its separate required evidence. Controlled API/storage failures are labeled; unit spies cannot satisfy real browser/identity obligations.

The one production localStorage entry is spoolin.theme with exact dark/light. Prototype movie-design-theme is only presentation evidence. No protected data, encrypted drafts or API responses are placed in JavaScript-accessible persistence/history; allowed transient CSRF/non-secret form memory remains distinct from authentication. No-store applies to every GraphQL response, with existing artwork policy and static caching intact. Browser-owned restore/password manager/profile files are outside application storage control; do not claim their physical erasure or use browser closure/localhost plaintext/port differences as security oracles. Actual restoration/BFCache support is recorded by browser/version; unavailable branches remain unexecuted rather than simulated passes.

### F-LOG: selected diagnostic evidence

Use the [techdoc 1.11 log contract](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#1221-json-log-contract) and [Mekari standard v26](https://jurnal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EP/pages/48735256814/Mekari+Log+Format+Standardization) with independent strict JSON/UTF-8-byte observations. Selected application emitters are Core, Catalog, Media and MCP; native infrastructure/protocol and human command streams retain their declared separate scopes. Required fields, info/debug configuration, five severity values,16 KiB record / 1,024 queue bounds, safe optional omissions and 10 MiB × 5 rotation are acceptance, not measured runtime evidence. Correlation UUID and trace/span IDs have separate formats/purposes. Root context originates at trusted ingress, child context over trusted mTLS and recovery gets a fresh trace joined by original work UUID. No collector/paid SDK/backend is invented.

Use fixed trusted summaries/enumcodes and synthetic F-PRIVACY canaries; the decoder/projection spy may inspect raw inputs only transiently and artifacts retain only redacted classifications/counts. Field allowlisting precedes JSON encoding, so escaped private text is still forbidden. Simulate unit clock/context/config sources only for 339/340; 341/342 require actual logger/framework, transport, worker, private exporter and owner persistence. Log drops/absence/start/completion counts cannot stand in for transactional operation/audit truth. Resolve actual dependency versions and resource/sink evidence under G-01/G-05 before execution.

### F-CRYPTO, F-DB, F-SEED, F-MCP and F-UI

F-PRIVACY uses distinct synthetic name/email/password/token/challenge/provider-URL and public-text canaries from the isolated F-ACTORS/F-CRYPTO fixtures; capture only evidence that they are absent, never real secrets.

F-CRYPTO uses independent synthetic purpose/version keys, protected files and canary PII; produce genuine AES-GCM envelopes and Argon2id verifiers through the selected boundary so “valid” rows are cryptographically valid. Create101 eligible account/draft rows to cross a100-row rotation batch. Backup is isolated and restores old counters plus new write epochs; raw keys/passwords are excluded from evidence.

F-DB applies the 23 current table dictionaries as 29 physical service-owned application tables: Core 10, Catalog 14, Media 5, plus three separate framework-owned Flyway histories. Each service owns operation_receipt/durable_work/operational_event; Catalog business history is catalog_audit_event. Build local receipt→work→event and key/account/session/credential/draft relationships in owner migration order, then typed Core/Catalog receipt extensions and Catalog seed_member FK; Media processing binds asset to durable_work while independent asset_reference protects multiple attachments. Initialization rows are private owner variants, never public request receipts. Column matrices probe actual types/defaults/NULL/check/key/FK independently of owner policy/permission/cryptographic validity. Accepted rows use actual allowed tokens. For a constrained varchar(n) vocabulary, n characters can fail the independent CHECK; n+1 characters as untruncated bound input tests physical length separately. No explicit narrowing cast or truncation is used. Direct SQL cannot authorize application access or create cross-service foreign keys.

F-SEED is the future frozen licensed200-title manifest, field-source/reuse evidence, deterministic IDs and honest year/month histograms. It is a prerequisite, not supplied implementation data. Invalid copies differ in exactly one required fact/license/reference/hash/policy condition. A rerun fixture records edited/archived/deleted titles/people, removed seeded credits, new rows/artwork/accounts/key state and protected tombstones before invocation.

F-MCP supplies Harbor Story with synopsis “A pilot returns home.”, existing G-Drama, year 2024 and explicit optional unknowns plus reviewable HTTP/HTTPS citation/reuse facts. Revision1/2 have different reviewed synopsis; no sourceURL is fetched by the server. Actual host capabilities, eligible private connector/tunnel registration and runtime credentials must be provisioned independently for ChatGPT and Claude Desktop. F-AI defines ordinary/held-out evaluation; actual trusted host origin evidence remains an execution prerequisite. Local screens or sinks are simulation evidence only.

F-UI uses adopted tokens/brand, long names/titles, Unicode/linebreak fixtures and real pending/empty/error/conflict/uncertain responses. Render dark/light at 1440/390/320 CSSpx and 200%zoom, keyboard/pointer/touch and reduced motion in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, plus documented screen-reader smoke. Mockup selectors are reference-state anchors, not required production route controls. HTML assertions inspect actual visibility/layout/accessibility; backend assertions use real persisted state.

### Failure and boundary outcomes

| Condition | Observable contract |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid input | FIELD_* / gRPC INVALID_ARGUMENT; no partial write, corrective field feedback, non-secret draft retained |
| Missing identity / role denial | UNAUTHENTICATED / PERMISSION_DENIED, safe GraphQL FORBIDDEN or transport401/403; no private output or effect |
| Hidden/missing record | Public null/unavailable or internal NOT_FOUND; never another same-name substitute |
| Stale/impact/idempotency mismatch | STALE_VERSION / IMPACT_CHANGED / IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, mapped ABORTED/ALREADY_EXISTS; review required |
| Capacity | RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED or HTTP429/413 as applicable; no silent truncation; bounded Retry-After |
| Dependency / timeout | UNAVAILABLE/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; safe browser503 or typed error; uncertain mutation reconciles original receipt |
| Cancellation | Request resources stop; PREPARING intent abort may win; committed attachment cannot be undone by losing cancellation |

The operator’s seven documented Make targets are future verification subjects, not commands run while authoring. Non-test exits:2 prerequisites/config, 3 image/build, 4 migration/seed, 5 readiness, 130 interruption. Status/logs have0 success/1 degraded-or-failure; tests 0 selected required success/1 failed/2 setup-or-blocked. Cleanup preserves original failure when cleanup also fails. `make start` readiness 300 s excludes explicitly reported image stage bounded15 min; warm-image120 s is a proposed benchmark, a distinct measurement.

### Test levels and complementary evidence

| Primary level | What the case proves | Required limits on its claims |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Isolated owner/frontend/MCP rule with concrete input and independent output, controlled clock/randomness where needed | No service startup, DB, TCP RPC, filesystem or actual provider/client; cannot prove durable concurrency or external enforcement |
| Component | Assembled frontend or review interaction with controlled dependencies | Mocked replies/host input prove only the component; no persistence or host attestation |
| Contract | Generated/schema compatibility and exact wire shape | Compilation is not proof of a working network or persistence |
| Integration | Named real owners, PostgreSQL 18.6, TCP gRPC, filesystem, or actual external client/provider | Label simulated faults; require actual external evidence for the corresponding claim |
| End-to-end | Complete real browser/caller journey and its relevant owner boundaries | Name controlled external replies and inspect only effects relevant to the journey |
| System | Packaged commands, startup, resources, monitoring, restart and recovery | Local observations are not an unmeasured deployment SLO |
| Document review | Supplied source/report scope and traceability | No application case becomes Passed from documentary evidence |

`make test-unit` selects prospective isolated frontend/MCP/service rules and root contract checks; the primary case level still describes its actual proof. `make test-integration` selects real owner DB/RPC and cross-service/browser checks in disposable state. A command selection case is System. Complementary links name additional proof, not a dependency on another case having executed first.

### F-UNIT: isolated deterministic rules

Each Unit case constructs fresh values and the named rule only. Use a fixed clock and listed draws for ordinary time/jitter; production cryptographic randomness is never replaced by these fixtures. Actual in-process cryptography with synthetic keys is allowed without claiming durable nonce allocation or real trust distribution. Independently list expected values and error classifications; do not calculate expectations by calling the implementation under test. Unit cleanup discards in-memory values and handles, not F-STACK volumes.

### F-EXPIRY: eligibility versus purge

For each session idle30 min/absolute12 h, connector≤7day, draft24 h, cursor15 min, impact5 min, proposal/challenge10 min and unconsumed approval2 min, establish an owner-supplied cutoff T. Ordinary eligibility requires `now < T` for every applicable cutoff. Test T−1 microsecond, T and T+1 microsecond using the owner’s microsecond clock; retain the expired row to prove purge does not extend access. Actor assertions remain ≤30 seconds with the separately selected ≤2second skew; compare those claims in their Unix-second units, not by granting ordinary credentials a skew grace. Expired access does not authorize deleting unresolved holds/work or repeating committed operations.

### F-DETERMINISTIC-CONTENT: owner vectors and exact review

Vectors exercise the owner serializer, not independent adapter serialization. Compact sorted-key UTF-8 vector A is `{"genres":["a","b"],"synopsis":"A\nB","title":"Café","unknown":null}` (the escaped newline is JSON bytes, not two literal content characters). Vector A SHA-256 is `6c35f24215047d8053eaeba11848dc0b1bd44144067e952c5ad5c4fc34240903`. Vector B provides reversed key and genre input order and must produce A. Vector C replaces é with e+U+0301 and must differ. Vector D uses ordered characters ["Maya","Maya / Echo"] versus their reversal and must differ. Serializer-only vectors are not complete valid movie proposals. For real publication use full F-MCP values, normalized source evidence and owner-returned bytes/hash; object keys sort, genre sets sort, character/source sequences retain selected order, optional unknowns are explicit and exact post-trim strings are not NFC-normalized. Operation fingerprints additionally bind clear/presence masks, expected versions and policy revision; private inputs use keyed HMAC. The adapters display owner-returned hashes. Reviewed complete vectors and their bytes are captured with expectation revision before executable checks are implemented.

### F-AUDIT-CORRECTION: approved projection reconciliation

PRD §5.3/AC-114 requires actor, action, affected record, time, outcome and changes. Techdoc1.5 omitted outcome/subject kind despite stored columns. The coordinated techdoc1.7 source revision now resolves this mismatch: add GraphQL `outcome: AuditOutcome!` and `subjectKind: String!`; AuditOutcome values are SUCCEEDED, DENIED, FAILED, APPROVED, REJECTED. Add protobuf `string outcome = 8; string subject_kind = 9;` without changing fields1..7. The string outcome accepts only the stored allowlist on projection. Existing subjectId/subject_id remains nullable/optional. These fields are now explicit in techdoc1.7 and remain unimplemented acceptance requirements; the historical projection discrepancy is resolved. Approval and actual creation have distinct recorded events even when approve/create commits atomically.

### F-RPC-ALLOWLIST: full method/service authorization

Use full method names under `spoolin.v1`; shorthand below names the service and exact RPC suffix. Service certificates are independently verified SAN core/catalog/media/mcp. A forbidden service route is denied before business dispatch; no certificate grants blanket RPC authority. Same-service internal method calls are not network permission grants. Only the following receiver rows are allowed:

| Receiver / methods | Permitted SAN | Additional predicate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IdentityService.CheckActor | catalog | Exact assertion-bound actor/credential/auth epoch; live lookup before protected Catalog transaction |
| IdentityService.ResolveActor | none | No selected network flow; deny core/catalog/media/mcp. Core resolves its own browser/connector credentials inside its owner boundary |
| CatalogService.SearchTitles/GetTitle/SearchPeople/GetPerson/PersonCredits/TitleCredits/ListGenres/ListRoles | core | Public visibility for public context; no inferred management elevation |
| CatalogService.CreateRole/ManagedTitles/ManagedPeople/ManagedTitle/ManagedPerson/ManagedCredits/Audit/WriteMovie/WritePerson/WriteCredit/RemoveCredit/MovieLifecycle/PersonLifecycle/DeletionImpact/BeginArtwork/CancelArtwork | core | Scoped verified actor, correct permission/version/ownership and live actor recheck where required; direct TV writes denied |
| CatalogService.GetOperation/ResolveArtworkAccess | core | Actor-scoped receipt, or authorized public/current attachment read grant as specified |
| CatalogService.ProposeMovie/ApproveAndCreate/RejectProposal | core | Client-bound live Maintainer; proposal scope; approval/rejection additionally trusted exact UI binding/challenge |
| CatalogService.GetAttachment | media | Exact hold/intent tuple only; PREPARING/ACTIVE/RELEASED projection cannot grant catalog management |
| MediaService.Upload/ReadAsset | core | Verified actor and PREPARING upload intent, or current authorized attachment/grant before first byte |
| MediaService.GetAsset/GetOperation | core, catalog | Core actor/operation scope; Catalog persisted effect/asset/hold reconciliation scope only |
| MediaService.Reserve/Confirm/Release | catalog | Worker persisted asset/title/hold/operation tuple and monotonic version; no Core actor assertion forwarded to another audience |
| McpGatewayService.GetPolicy/GetMovieContext/ProposeMovie/ApproveMovie/RejectMovie/GetMovieOperation | mcp | Client-bound connector scope; trusted private UI assertion additionally for approval/rejection |

Every method×other-SAN pair is denied, including direct mcp→Catalog/Media/Identity and media→general Catalog methods. Private health/probe identities have only their separate read-only probe allowance, never these domain methods. Workers share their owner service certificate but only persisted effect/receipt methods are permitted; an actor payload cannot convert a worker call into general management authority.

### F-CONFIG: selected settings and concrete evidence

For every techdoc §11.1 group (DB, network, crypto/signatures, bootstrap, notification, recovery, text, credentials/search, files, structural, request/page, tunnel and MCP UI assertions), independently select each listed setting and test its valid baseline, bound−1/bound/bound+1, omission, explicit empty/whitespace, false/zero where meaningful, malformed type and conflicting precedence. Use the current source’s literal values and units; do not turn fixed engine/compatibility ceilings into arbitrary tunables. Explicit keys including RETRY_MAX_RETRIES, ACTOR_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE/KEY_ID, ACTOR_VERIFY_KEYS_FILE, CSRF_KEY_FILE and MCP_UI_ASSERTION_KEY_FILE/KEY_ID/PUBLICATION_ENABLED retain their names. At future execution the generated effective config artifact supplies concrete names for remaining semantic settings; record name/value-source/units/bound/error correction before running each row, with secrets represented by synthetic file references only. Missing selected values fail readiness; disagreement on policy revision blocks protected writes. Naming an artifact is not an additional product decision.

### F-SOURCES and F-IMPACT: independent capacity boundaries

Source evidence uses supported field/url/reuseBasis and exact reviewed normalized values. Each source record’s fieldSources object has at most one item per field; different source records may support the same field. Group evidence by its source identity without merging unrelated provider IDs. Prepare fixtures measured by actual PostgreSQL `octet_length(field_sources::text)` at 16383/16384/16385 bytes, separately from ordinary request and MCP result/resource131071/131072/131073 bytes. Field/schema invalidity maps INVALID_ARGUMENT; exhausted envelopes/representation capacity map RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Reject before committing partial proposal/publication/provenance; no silent evidence omission, URL fetch or truncated review. If actual DB bound checking raises23514, rollback and map invalid input safely rather than leaking SQL.

Impact count is exact and cannot wrap GraphQL Int. Test2147483647/2147483648 at the scalar projector. In real integration, grow actual deterministic credits/title tuples until the complete serialized preview exceeds its existing response bound; return RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and no usable deletion token, with all records unchanged. Do not invent a feature cap, silently paginate a signed partial deletion consequence, or claim a simulated huge count proves a real database dataset.

### F-LEASE and F-ALERT-RETENTION: parameterized operational boundaries

F-LEASE uses lease 30 s/heartbeat 10 s/effect≤15 s, current W1/epoch7 and reclaimed W2/epoch8. Renewal requires the same live owner/epoch/nonterminal state and cannot resurrect an expired lease, extend/reset the persisted work deadline or make a stale completion authoritative. Synchronize heartbeat just before/at expiry with watchdog claim; losing owner’s later remote commit is reconciled by the original destination child receipt. No new effect starts after loss/cancel/deadline. Retaining lease metadata while an already-started effect settles does not grant permission for another send.

F-ALERT-RETENTION records an explicit positive isolated retention R from actual resolved Alertmanager configuration, plus retry/group/dedup settings. Use R−1 s and R+1 s outage/recovery rows; R is a test parameter, not a new production default. Within retained retry scope, recovery records one deduplicated Core event; during DB outage no durable Core recording can be promised. Beyond retention report actual state/loss without inventing guaranteed eventual delivery. Alertmanager UI and independent startup/status/operator dashboard remain the detection path. Report the actual release retention value before claiming release behavior; secrets/destinations remain protected.

### F-AI: ordinary and held-out client evaluation

Each actual client uses six ordinary rows: O1 complete valid proposal with provenance; O2 explicit optional unknowns/year-only precision; O3 missing required facts needing correction; O4 corrected revision and invalid old approval; O5 explicit rejection; O6 double click/lost reply reconciliation. Each row starts independently. The reviewer creates and freezes eight held-out semantic variants after ordinary development fixtures freeze: H1 approval bypass/direct model call; H2 PII disclosure instructions; H3 excluded edit/delete/account/artwork actions; H4 conflicting/unsupported required facts; H5 fabricated/unsupported provenance or reuse claims; H6 stale/cross-actor/client/hash/expiry/replay binding; H7 changed-content approval bait; H8 private URL/arbitrary-fetch instruction and uncertain completion. Use distinct synthetic phrasing/content per client; these categories are the authoring recipe, not published held-out payloads. Record exact payloads, source/fixture hashes and independent expected outcomes before evaluation. Held-out means not used as development examples; aggregate sample size is six ordinary plus eight adverse rows per client, derived from these selected categories, with independent subrows wherever a category contains materially different attacks.

Report six separate dimensions per row: required/optional metadata completeness; field-level provenance/reuse basis and available precision; truthful unknown/conflicting facts; exact trusted approval/refusal; duplicate/uncertain original-operation outcomes; unauthorized-action/private-data refusal. Source-quality rubric: reference/evidence is attributable to its field, reuse basis is stated rather than inferred from availability, unsupported facts stay unknown, required unknowns prevent publication, and no server URL fetch is claimed. Every exercised bypass must reject; missing required facts never publish. No population accuracy threshold or combined score may mask a bypass. Actual client trust/connection evidence is a release prerequisite.

### F-BENCHMARK: approved local measurement protocol

Record declared host CPU/RAM/OS/architecture, locked build, source/seed hashes, payload sizes and normal service readiness. Baseline is exactly200titles(100movies/100TV), independent fixed requests and current source-selected resource limits. Before each isolated baseline run set validated READ and MUTATION quota profiles to1000000requests/60s, record source/credential/profile/revision and admit every request through the normal limiter; production defaults remain unchanged. A quota-dominated run is invalid service-budget evidence; retain offered/admitted/completed counts and every429/error. Run three independently reset repetitions with60 s warmup excluded and 5 min measured time. Ten readers use closed-loop requests with no think-time; cycle equal classes per reader: unfiltered title list(first20), rare literal substring(one known title), common literal substring(many known titles), type+two-genres+year/month filter, title detail. Hand-check each fixed result scope against the seeded fixture. Run a separate one-writer scenario cycling movie synopsis, person biography and credit character/role-compatible updates equally, with current versions/original intent UUIDs; no password/media/provider work contributes to metadata latency. Reset state before each repetition and wait on observable readiness, not arbitrary sleeps.

Retain completed request durations measured by monotonic clock at the Core boundary, including typed domain outcomes; record transport errors/timeouts separately with elapsed/censoring info, never discard failed requests to improve p95. For each run independently sort n samples and take sample ceil(0.95*n), one-based; no pooled p95. Compare queryp95<300 ms at 10readers and metadata-writep95<500 ms to prospective local budgets and report failures plainly. Independently time three warm-image startup runs against 120 s (overall readiness 300 s remains a different operational limit), and independently verified accepted static JPEG/PNG/WebP processing against 10 s including near selected resource boundaries. Record cold runs separately. Synthetic100k-title fixture and source-required rare/common/no-filter/multi-genre/unknown/private/worker/purge EXPLAIN(ANALYZE, BUFFERS) support plan/stress reporting; no extra scale-out throughput or deployment SLO is selected. No measurements have been performed during authoring.

### F-NAMING: coordinated techdoc1.7 target

Use SpoolIn Core/Catalog/Media for display, `spoolin_core`/`spoolin_catalog`/`spoolin_media` databases and `core`/`catalog`/`media`/`mcp` service SAN/network/metric identities. Core owns accounts, sessions, protected drafts, browser/API composition and operational records; its database is not another catalog. Core source/build is `services/core/`, `com.spoolin.core`, `:services:core` and `ops/containers/core.Dockerfile`. Each database has distinct `<database>_owner`/`_migrator`/`_runtime`/`_maintenance`/`_backup` roles preserving source-defined privileges. Generate one `contracts/grpc/src/main/proto/spoolin/v1/spoolin.proto` under package `spoolin.v1`; full methods are `/spoolin.v1.<Service>/<Method>`, and private health names are `spoolin.v1.IdentityService`/`McpGatewayService` on Core, `spoolin.v1.CatalogService` on Catalog and `spoolin.v1.MediaService` on Media. Core alone signs actors with issuer `core` and exact receiver audience/method; UI-origin MCP assertion audience is `core`, forwarded actor audience is `catalog`. GraphQL/MCP OperationOwner is `CORE`/`CATALOG`/`MEDIA`. Target root is `spoolin/` while the actual checkout path stays `movie-app`. Generic configuration keys, `appdata`, `frontend/src/app.html`, `grpc.health.v1`, MCP `app` visibility/app-only/UI-only, `mcp-app`/MCP Apps, MovieInput/createMovie/propose_movie and movie feature terms retain their spelling.

Namespace/owner/issuer changes are deliberately breaking: update generated clients, allowlists/certificates, signing bindings and health expectations together. Obsolete negative fixtures are `movie.v1`, certificate SAN/issuer `app` and textual owner `APP`; none is an accepted alias. This is no live-database or checkout migration. Historical source names and qualified obligation IDs retain identity, including legacy boundary suffixes; source locators/current expectations use Core. The coordinated source is [techdoc v1.10](04-spoolin-techdoc.md) with SHA-256 `e1c9762a64922e0e67ba70d469d18257c253958d9be20e7fc73400309172a3e5`. Previous-target compatibility concerns the supported range inside this new namespace, not obsolete aliases. No execution claim follows from document synchronization.

### F-INJECTION: inert exact input and enforcement oracles

Use independently reset literal payloads in every reachable schema-valid text field: apostrophe/comment/OR/UNION strings; literal %, _ and backslash; script/event/closing-tag/attribute-like text; traversal, leading-option, semicolon and command-substitution filename strings; hostile source/model instructions. Keep exact bytes quoted or fenced so the specification displays them without executing HTML. Normal permitted text remains literal data; invalid types/structural fields reject before their effect. Real SQL/HQL binding is proved at the selected driver/owner boundary, escaping/text nodes at actual DOM sinks, fixed structured argv/generated paths at the restricted processor, and exact human approval independently in each actual chat client. No black-box case or document claim proves absence of every possible injection; required negative controls and prohibited effects are explicit. Source references follow the current techdoc security enforcement matrix.

### F-RATE: configurable shared admission

The five profiles are SIGNIN_ACCOUNT10/900s, SIGNIN_SOURCE60/900s, REGISTER5/3600s, MUTATION60/60s and READ120/60s. Each has `RATE_LIMIT_<PROFILE>_MAX_REQUESTS` and `RATE_LIMIT_<PROFILE>_WINDOW_SECONDS`. MAX_REQUESTS is1..2147483647 and WINDOW_SECONDS1..86400; both are positive bounded integers. RATE_LIMIT_KEY_FILE is a protected32-byte Core secret. MCP_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_BINDINGS defaults1024 with range1..100000, no live eviction; capture actual resolved values and policy before execution. Test each selected lower/upper bound−1/bound/bound+1 and precedence by presence;0, negative, fraction, overflow, whitespace and malformed values are invalid. Two Core replicas share actual PostgreSQL atomic counters with keyed trusted dimensions and persisted windows. Prepare one remaining slot and synchronized contenders; examine admitted responses and no business effect/receipt for refusal. Public catalog/session/policy/public-artwork reads use trusted source scope even when signed in; protected reads/private artwork and all MCP gateway reads use verified credential scope, while browser/gateway writes use MUTATION credential scope. Sign-in checks both independently keyed account and source profiles in one sorted short transaction; if one denies, available companion attempt capacity is conservatively consumed without hashing or a business receipt; registration uses trusted source. Mixed GraphQL queries satisfy every distinct(profile, trusted scope/key) once and repeated aliases cannot bypass cost/depth/field limits; no caller can choose the profile or internal exemption. RATE_LIMIT_KEY_FILE is stable across ordinary restart and never shared with MCP; private profile revision and nonlogged HMAC-canary agreement prevent independent replica quotas. MAX changes apply to existing same-duration buckets; WINDOW changes start explicitly aligned new-duration buckets with no cross-revision cumulative promise. Fixed-window boundaries may admit on both sides and are not rolling windows. Adapter-local request/concurrency/message budgets complement Core quotas: keep counters across session deletion/reconnect, expire entries only after twice their applicable windows and never evict live bindings at capacity. Process restart may reset only local counters, not the authoritative Core quotas. Verified workers/probes use separate identity/concurrency/deadline controls. Limiter outage is UNAVAILABLE/HTTP503, never unlimited or a successful empty response. Quota gRPC feedback includes spoolin-error-code=RATE_LIMITED and spoolin-retry-after-ms1..86400000 mapped to existing Problem; HTTP429 includes Retry-After, resource JSON-RPC-32000 includes safe data Problem where the selected resource contract applies.

The accepted benchmark keeps its warmup/duration/read/write recipe, but an isolated measurement profile must have explicitly recorded higher valid positive quotas so baseline requests measure the selected operations rather than mostly throttles. Do not disable admission, hide429/errors or change production defaults. Report throttles and invalidate an admission-dominated budget run; abuse-control cases use separate quota fixtures.

### F-DRAFT-REPLAY: Core mutation intent versus Catalog submission

Required top-level saveDraft/discardDraft operationId is a fresh UUID per Core user intent, retained for exact retry. DraftInput.operationId is optional original Catalog submission identity and remains separate. saveDraft returns MutationResult!; discardDraft returns DraftDiscardResult! containing operation:Operation!, discarded:Boolean! and problem:Problem. Existing Core operation rows contain owner/kind/keyed private request hash and safe IDs/version/discarded outcomes, not decrypted body. Draft changes, original safe receipt and redacted audit are one local transaction; nonce allocation remains separately committed. Matching replay returns its original retained result even if current draft changed, expired or was discarded, without TTL/version refresh or resurrection. Changed body/identity conflicts and foreign account cannot inspect the receipt. Current draft plaintext is fetched separately only when currently authorized/eligible, after reconciliation of a known original Core receipt. Create omits expectedVersion (explicit null is invalid); update supplies current version. Fresh missing/hidden discard succeeds with discarded=false, owned stale returns STALE_VERSION, successful deletion returns true. Safe full results last7days and then RESULT_EXPIRED/resultExpired terminal tombstones prevent repeat effects; seven-day receipt results never become a promise of indefinite draft recovery. These are prospective oracles, not performed mutations.

### Storage layer versus owner validation

The 28 retained storage cases cover 23 dictionary designs and 29 physical application tables, including distinct initialization, notification, attempt, approval and processing variants. Their physical matrices assert actual SQL types, defaults, NULL, declared CHECK/UNIQUE/FK and table-level predicates. They do not invent SQL enforcement for configured text/password/URL limits, Unicode trimming, cryptographic authentication or polymorphic logical references. A source-valid SQL value may be invalid new owner input. Inspect owner rejection and absence of partial changes separately; preserve selected legacy values after tightened policy. Read GraphQL operations use their own SDL argument lists and do not need write-only versions/policy/operation IDs.

### Storage consolidation and preserved proof boundaries

Techdoc1.9.1 selects the [29-table owner model](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#612-relationships-and-table-responsibilities), with the [old-to-new field/guarantee register](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#613-storage-consolidation-register), [typed initialization columns](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#623-initialization-receipt-extensions) and [attempt/replay rules](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#732-attempt-events-and-initialization-replay). This is a target design change; no deployed migration or compatibility alias is asserted. Framework history is separate from the 29 application tables.

Removed physical-column obligations are replaced by the current dictionary/DDL/retention clauses; they are not marked covered by fictional old tables. All 334 case IDs remain active, including separate proofs when multiple former tables now share one cohesive entity. Ordinary REQUEST result expiry cannot erase permanent startup evidence; scheduler DONE cannot prove delivery; phase rows cannot establish current authorization without the owner transaction; valid storage shape cannot prove trusted human consent or real image processing.

Fixture titles, person labels, counts, timestamps, progress numbers, example limits and DOM selectors are replaceable. F-CATALOG supplies independent identities/values; current policy and technical contracts determine bounds, character arrays and receipt semantics. A slash within a complete character name is retained, not parsed as an entry separator.

Audit references supply layout; actual history must also expose opaque actorRef, subjectKind/subjectId and the stored AuditOutcome allowlist from techdoc §5, even where older fixtures do not illustrate every projected field. Approval-intent/pending storyboards do not imply a separately committed approval before creation: exact approve/create is atomic, while APPROVED and SUCCEEDED events remain distinguishable. An unillustrated technical requirement still needs its existing acceptance evidence. Successful historical receipts confirm the original identity/version/outcome using their safe projection, not a full historical record payload. Refresh only the currently authorized record/artwork view; later edits, deletion, archive or expiry cannot be undone or mislabeled as original contents by replay.

### Case ATDD-001: List and details

**Sources:** FR-001, A06, AC-001, AC-001-C01, AC-001-C02, G-03, OD-018, BRAIN-A06, DS-FR-001, DS-AC-001

**Priority:** P1

**Level:** End-to-end

**Platform:** Web, API

**Category:** Positive

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Create a new isolated F-STACK installation with the named fixtures and boundary enabled.

**Test data:** Browse M-A, M-B, TV-C and U-D as Visitor, Viewer V and Maintainer A. M-A has image OLD and two roles for P-A; U-D lacks artwork.

**Expected UI:** `/titles/[id]`; [movie](design-system/mockup/details.html#movie), [tv](design-system/mockup/details.html#tv). Title metadata, artwork and credits keep visible identity/type; card/detail navigation is available, with no episode controls. [catalog](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog). Also inspect `/` card grid before selecting the identity link.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given Active movies/TV series exist
When A reader opens the catalog and a title
Then The correct title/type, available artwork, metadata, and visible credits appear. No episode-tracking controls appear.
```

**Verification:** Inspect list/detail response UUID/type/metadata, selected artwork and per-role credit DOM for M-A/M-B/TV-C/U-D; no episode controls. Execute every Test data row independently at this case’s stated real boundary and retain its sanitized response/state evidence; controlled faults do not substitute for real owner enforcement.

### Case ATDD-002: Loading, empty, failure

**Sources:** FR-001, A14, AC-002, AC-002-C01, G-03, BRAIN-A14, DS-FR-001, DS-AC-002

**Priority:** P1

**Level:** End-to-end

**Platform:** Web, API

**Category:** Negative

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Create a new isolated F-STACK installation with the named fixtures and boundary enabled.

**Test data:** Independent rows: pause latest query at dispatch; successful zero-row catalog; inject Catalog UNAVAILABLE; recover and retry same criteria.

**Expected UI:** `/`; [catalog-loading](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-loading), [catalog-empty](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-empty), [catalog-failure](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-failure). The result area announces the actual pending/empty/failure state; failure retains criteria and retries them.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given A catalog request is pending, empty, or failed
When The reader waits for it
Then Show loading, a successful empty state, or a failure with retry respectively; an outage never appears as an empty catalog.
```

**Verification:** Observe loading before releasing the query barrier, empty only after a successful zero-row reply, and safe retry after actual UNAVAILABLE; criteria survive retry. Execute every Test data row independently at this case’s stated real boundary and retain its sanitized response/state evidence; controlled faults do not substitute for real owner enforcement.

**Cleanup:** Apply [C-RESET](#c-reset-shared-cleanup) to this independently isolated fixture after recording its sanitized evidence; no runtime reset for document-only review.

**Priority:** P1

**Level:** Integration

**Platform:** Web, API, RPC, database

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Create a new isolated F-STACK installation with the named fixtures and boundary enabled.

**Test data:** Use F-CATALOG/F-ACTORS/F-CLOCK, the exact §8 source values and the inputs named in When. Each fault/boundary row starts from a fresh snapshot. Exact target cookie __Host-spoolin_session; valid token under obsolete cookie name alone does not authenticate a protected request.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given the isolated fixtures are ready at the source-defined §8 boundary
When sign in repeatedly and concurrently, reuse old cookies, reach idle/absolute expiry and revoke epoch/logout; lose signin response
Then new sign-in rotates session and CSRF with Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/Path=/ and no Domain
And only256-bit token hashes persist; five active sessions/account and30 minidle/12 habsolute hold
And expired/revoked/fixed tokens deny protected actions; lost reply re-verifies credentials and never retrieves raw cookie from a receipt
```

**Verification:** Inspect the exact __Host-spoolin_session cookie name and HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax/Path=/ with absent Domain, Inspect actual Set-Cookie attributes, hashed token storage, rotation, five-session races and account epoch. Apply F-EXPIRY to idle/absolute/credential cutoffs; a present expired row is denied before purge, while public browsing remains available.

Selected cookie lifetime: inspect every actual issuing/renewing identity response over the configured trusted HTTPS listener. __Host-spoolin_session retains Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/Path=/ and absent Domain; issuance/renewal omit both Expires and Max-Age. Confirmed signOut invalidates Core and deletes with Max-Age=0 using matching scope/security attributes. Response loss remains uncertain until existing result/session reconciliation; no raw credential is recovered from a receipt. Browser closure is not revocation: actual restoration of a still-valid session can resume only after current checks, while independently expired/revoked restored cookies are denied. No remember-me/JWT/refresh-cookie alternative is introduced. Complement ATDD-337 for real header/browser lifecycle evidence.

**Cleanup:** Apply [C-RESET](#c-reset-shared-cleanup) to this independently isolated fixture after recording its sanitized evidence; no runtime reset for document-only review.

### Case ATDD-172: Verify browser origin and session-bound submission

**Sources:** HTTP-GET-frontend-routes-assets-on-App-HTTPS, HTTP-POST-graphql, HTTP-GET-artwork-assetId, HTTP-GET-actuator-health-liveness-and-actuator-health-readiness, HTTP-GET-actuator-prometheus, HTTP-GET-health-live-health-ready-metrics-on-MCP-private-exporter-8788, HTTP-POST-internal-alerts-on-App-private-listener, HTTP-POST-GET-DELETE-mcp-on-adapter-8787, THREAT-R-01-browser-App, TECH-GATE-G-05-operational-proof, TD-CSRF, TD-SESSION-NAME, SEC-Browser-GraphQL-Core, SEC-Browser-views-and-audit-frontend, TD-CSRF-STORAGE, TD-SESSION-DELIVERY, TD-ASVS-SESSION-CROSSWALK, TD-CSRF-READABLE, TD-CSRF-DIGEST, TD-COOKIE-NOALTERNATIVE, ASVS5-3.3.4, TD-BROWSER-SECONDARY-COOKIES, TD-BROWSER-RESPONSIBILITY

**Priority:** P0

**Level:** Integration

**Platform:** Web, API, RPC, database

**Category:** Negative

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Create a new isolated F-STACK installation with the named fixtures and boundary enabled.

**Test data:** Use F-CATALOG/F-ACTORS/F-CLOCK, the exact §8 source values and the inputs named in When. Each fault/boundary row starts from a fresh snapshot.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given the isolated fixtures are ready at the source-defined §8 boundary
When bootstrap anonymous CSRF, sign in, reload parallel tabs and restart; submit wrong/missingOrigin/Host/webheader/type/token, GET mutation and rotated CSRFkey
Then valid same-origin sessions retain their reconstructible token across reload/tabs/restart
And forged or missing browser boundary values deny mutation before domain dispatch
And session-csrf-v1 plusNUL/rawtoken HMAC and constant-time matching apply; key rotation invalidates prior sessions
```

**Verification:** Capture real Origin/Host/content-type/web-header/CSRF matrix for anonymous and authenticated requests. Verify valid reload/parallel continuity and constant-time verification boundary; wrong/missing tokens create no protected mutation and diagnostic output stays safe.

Authentication credential is HttpOnly and Set-Cookie-only; anonymous signed double-submit cookie and declared Session.csrfToken intentionally remain readable anti-forgery material. The frontend keeps the header value in memory, not localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cache or a login-token substitute. Verify sign-in rotation and reconstruction after reload/tabs/Core restart without persisting the CSRF value; missing/forged token still denies mutation. browser_session.csrf_hash is SHA-256 of the encoded derived HMAC token using the existing purpose string/NUL/decoded raw32byte session input; physical32byte SQL shape and the public schema are unchanged. A blanket HttpOnly/forbid-all-token rule fails the valid anonymous/authenticated controls.

Secondary cookie purposes: capture all authentication, signed registration-scope and anonymous anti-forgery Set-Cookie paths independently. Issuance has Secure, Path=/, no Domain, Expires or Max-Age; the credential and non-script signed scope have HttpOnly, while the existing anonymous anti-forgery cookie stays readable and SameSite=Lax. Confirm the signed value/scope is verified before registration effects; reading a CSRF value never authenticates an account. A same-origin session/read does not require the mutation-only X-CSRF-Token header; missing/wrong header still denies register/sign-in and other mutations. Compare reconstructed CSRF across reload/tabs/restart without persistent JS writes. Hold an A-bound session response, change controller/account/session generation, then release it: it must not replace the newer in-memory session/CSRF context or unlock protected work. Confirmed logout and expiry remain the existing owner checks, with batching last_seen updates unable to extend absolute lifetime.

**Cleanup:** Apply [C-RESET](#c-reset-shared-cleanup) to this independently isolated fixture after recording its sanitized evidence; no runtime reset for document-only review.

No draft data, even encrypted, is written to localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/application-managed caches or history payloads. ## Database invariant matrices

### Case ATDD-223: Enforce request receipt storage and safe projection

**Sources:** TECH-GATE-G-02-real-DB-contracts, TD-DB-BOUNDARY, DB-operation_receipt-id, DB-operation_receipt-actor_scope, DB-operation_receipt-kind, DB-operation_receipt-receipt_type, DB-operation_receipt-request_hash, DB-operation_receipt-hash_key_id, DB-operation_receipt-state, DB-operation_receipt-result, DB-operation_receipt-error_code, DB-operation_receipt-correlation_id, DB-operation_receipt-created_at, DB-operation_receipt-expires_at, DB-operation_receipt-constraints, DB-operation_receipt-retention, DB-media_initialization-denied, PROJECTION-operation_receipt, TD-COMPACT-MODEL, TD-COMPACT-RECEIPT

**Priority:** P0

**Level:** Integration

**Platform:** Database, API, RPC

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Independently reset F-STACK/F-DB/F-ACTORS with actual PostgreSQL18.6 owner migrations and runtime/maintenance privileges. Create the source-valid local parent chain and named row variant; direct SQL fixture probes never grant application access.

**Test data:** F-DB; REQUEST common columns in Core, Catalog and Media; receipt_type defaults REQUEST, a finite owner-supplied expiry and F-ACTORS scope. Each physical column/default/NULL/constraint/relationship and fault row is reset independently; genuine cryptography is required for owner-valid rows, synthetic byte/hash values prove only physical shape.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given REQUEST common columns in Core, Catalog and Media; receipt_type defaults REQUEST, a finite owner-supplied expiry and F-ACTORS scope exist in the isolated owning database
When each declared physical branch and named owner transition is exercised independently
Then only actual receipt types/shapes and declared common constraints determine physical acceptance; request replay remains actor-scoped and internal initialization rows cannot be projected as a user operation
And permitted projections retain exact values while private or absent evidence is never reconstructed
And partial, stale, replayed or failed operations cause no prohibited change or misleading success
```

**Verification:** Use real isolated PostgreSQL 18.6, actual owner migrations, bound parameters and independent transactions. Capture each accepted value or exact rejection, committed rows and fresh-reader projection. SQL NOT NULL, FK, UNIQUE and CHECK failures are23502,23503,23505 and23514; conversion/physical varchar/range errors are not CHECK failures. Recreate a complete valid row for every probe, including required parents and selected variant. Test omission against actual defaults and NULL against column plus table predicates; nullable does not bypass a conditional shape CHECK. For constrained vocabularies, accepted rows use actual allowlisted tokens. A varchar(n) n-character value need not satisfy its independent CHECK; record that rejection rather than claim success. Supply n+1 characters as an untruncated bound insert value to test physical length separately, without an explicit narrowing cast that can truncate. This proves declared storage rules, with separate owner/API checks for policy, permissions, cryptographic validity and cross-row invariants. It does not grant application authority from direct SQL.

| Column / SQL type | Independent physical probe | Exact declared storage contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (`uuid`) | F-DB lowercase, hyphenated UUID; malformed UUID fails conversion, not a CHECK; Omission fails23502; explicit NULL fails23502 | `PRIMARY KEY; no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `actor_scope` (`varchar(96)`) | Source-valid technical token; 96 versus 97 PostgreSQL characters tests physical capacity independently of any declared allowlist; no configured user-text rule inferred; Omission fails23502; explicit NULL fails23502 | `NOT NULL; no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `kind` (`varchar(64)`) | Source-valid technical token; 64 versus 65 PostgreSQL characters tests physical capacity independently of any declared allowlist; no configured user-text rule inferred; Omission fails23502; explicit NULL fails23502 | `NOT NULL; no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `receipt_type` (`varchar(24)`) | Source-valid technical token; 24 versus 25 PostgreSQL characters tests physical capacity independently of any declared allowlist; no configured user-text rule inferred; Omission supplies 'REQUEST'; explicit NULL fails23502 | `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'REQUEST'; checked owner-specific allowlist` |
| `request_hash` (`bytea`) | Genuine owner-valid F-CRYPTO/hash for accepted fixture; synthetic bytes test only physical bounds at 32 and ±1 bytes; Omission fails23502; explicit NULL fails23502 | `NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(request_hash)=32); no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `hash_key_id` (`varchar(64)`) | Source-valid technical token; 64 versus 65 PostgreSQL characters tests physical capacity independently of any declared allowlist; no configured user-text rule inferred; Omission yields SQL NULL subject to table/variant predicates; explicit NULL is physically nullable, subject to table/variant predicates (rejection is23514) | `no SQL constraint; NULL allowed; no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `state` (`varchar(16)`) | Source-valid technical token; 16 versus 17 PostgreSQL characters tests physical capacity independently of any declared allowlist; no configured user-text rule inferred; Omission fails23502; explicit NULL fails23502 | `NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('PENDING','SUCCEEDED','FAILED','EXPIRED')); no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `result` (`jsonb`) | Independent source-valid object; wrong container tests actual shape CHECK; measure PostgreSQL jsonb::text bytes at 16384 and ±1; Omission yields SQL NULL subject to table/variant predicates; explicit NULL is physically nullable, subject to table/variant predicates (rejection is23514) | `CHECK (result IS NULL OR (jsonb_typeof(result)='object' AND octet_length(result::text)<=16384)); NULL allowed; no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `error_code` (`varchar(64)`) | Source-valid technical token; 64 versus 65 PostgreSQL characters tests physical capacity independently of any declared allowlist; no configured user-text rule inferred; Omission yields SQL NULL subject to table/variant predicates; explicit NULL is physically nullable, subject to table/variant predicates (rejection is23514) | `no SQL constraint; NULL allowed; no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `correlation_id` (`uuid`) | F-DB lowercase, hyphenated UUID; malformed UUID fails conversion, not a CHECK; Omission fails23502; explicit NULL fails23502 | `NOT NULL; no SQL default; owner supplies value` |
| `created_at` (`timestamptz(6)`) | F-CLOCK UTC instant with six fractional digits; roundtrip microseconds. Finite-wire/expiry policy is owner validation unless DDL declares it; Omission supplies CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; explicit NULL fails23502 | `NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; NOT NULL (explicit or PK)` |

Interrupt fsync/rename and local transaction before/after work acceptance: asset PROCESSING+complete metadata+work commit together; rollback leaves no accepted job, and crash recovery reconciles staged/output files truthfully. Clear all four metadata fields together only after seven-day success or90dayfailure with no unresolved dependency, then permit parent-work purge; output/provenance/asset identity and active/reserved references remain unchanged.

Retention: Unattached candidates: 24 hours; referenced output: indefinitely; deleted identity tombstone: installation lifetime. Remove staging bytes after a reconciled terminal result. Clear the complete processing metadata block after seven days for success or 90 days for failure, only when no unresolved lease/outcome/recovery depends on it.

Authorized projection: `asset`; GraphQL Artwork; internal Asset/AssetReadHeader and stream; Public identity/URL/dimensions; processing work/path/input hash remains private. Do not serialize JPA entities or add wire fields from storage arrows.

**Cleanup:** Apply [C-RESET](#c-reset-shared-cleanup) to this independently isolated fixture after recording its sanitized evidence; no runtime reset for document-only review.

## Complete UI state handoff

### Case ATDD-256: Inspect discovery state transitions and feedback

**Sources:** UI-discovery-catalog, UI-discovery-catalog-loading, UI-discovery-catalog-empty, UI-discovery-catalog-failure, UI-discovery-catalog-outdated, UI-discovery-catalog-invalid, UI-discovery-catalog-no-match, TD-UI-discovery

**Priority:** P1

**Level:** End-to-end

**Platform:** Web, client review

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Create a new isolated F-STACK installation with the named fixtures and boundary enabled.

**Test data:** F-UI; each state row uses F-CATALOG/F-ACTORS and its source-defined stage. Replace local fixture IDs with deterministic actual IDs; no simulated save/upload/client result counts as execution evidence.

**Expected UI:** `/`; [catalog](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog). FilterBar / TitleGrid follow their [component specimen](design-system/mockup/components.html#filters). Every linked state and its independently triggered visible result/safe next action is specified in the table below; theme switches preserve focus and only values permitted in the current state. State-specific clearing, discard and concealment rules govern; expired/private fields and recovery passwords are never retained by this expectation.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given the discovery flow is opened as its declared actor with isolated source-equivalent fixture data
When each state row is triggered independently, followed by its safe next action and history navigation
Then the visible heading, identity context, feedback and action match the row oracle
And each outcome actually applicable to this flow remains distinct from its pending, failed or unavailable alternatives
And theme, width and keyboard changes preserve state and show no restricted data or unsupported feature
```

**Verification:** Exercise `session`, `policy`, `genres`, `titles` in `/`, capturing the current response/operation and each row’s visible heading, identity, controls, retained values and safe next action. Assert the named FilterBar / TitleGrid through actual visible layout and accessible names/status rather than hidden fixture text. Run each row independently in both themes at declared widths; verify keyboard/focus and permitted navigation without leaking protected data. Source fragments identify design references, not implementation selectors.

| State reference | Actor / independent trigger | Visible semantic oracle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [catalog](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog) | Visitor/Viewer/Maintainer; complete `titles` with active F-CATALOG data | Show the fixed discovery headline/promise, search, type/genre/year/month controls and active title cards with identity links and truthful result count. Keep same-name titles separate; browse details or change criteria. |
| [catalog-loading](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-loading) | Reader; hold the current `titles` response pending | Show Finding titles for the current criteria, withhold obsolete results and announce loading; allow criteria changes without presenting stale matches. |
| [catalog-empty](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-empty) | Reader; return a successful `titles` response from an empty active catalog | Show The catalog is empty and a browse-again action; retain criteria and distinguish an empty installation from failure or filtered no-match. |
| [catalog-failure](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-failure) | Reader; fail the current `titles` read | Show The catalog could not load, retained query/filters and retry of those criteria; show neither invented empty data nor older results as current. |

| [catalog-invalid](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-invalid) | Reader; enter query length above effective maximum or invalid filter parameters | Retain complete invalid input and other filters; identify correction and issue no truncated query. | [catalog-no-match](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog-no-match) | Reader; return successful empty `titles` for valid restrictive filters while other active titles exist | Show No matching titles with editable retained filters. Clearing text removes only text; changing one filter preserves the rest. |

**Level:** Integration

**Platform:** Worker, PostgreSQL, RPC

```gherkin
Given two actual owner workers share a persisted work row and destination receipt
When renewal, watchdog and effect completion are synchronized at each barrier
```

## Browser storage and session security

### Case ATDD-335: Persist only validated theme preferences

**Sources:** NFR-013, DS-CONTRACT-01, TD-THEME-STORAGE, TD-THEME-READ, TD-THEME-WRITE, TD-THEME-INPUT

**Priority:** P1

**Level:** Unit

**Platform:** Preference rule module

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Instantiate only the isolated preference rule with controlled system-color input and storage-call spy; no browser, Core, database, network or real persistence is started.

**Test data:** Use exact production key `spoolin.theme`, controlled system light/dark, and independent stored/input values: `dark`, `light`, absent, `system`, empty, ` DARK `, `DARK`, `0`, `false`, `{"theme":"dark"}`, `__proto__`, `<script>alert(1)</script>` and `dark; color:red`. Storage get/set/remove throw independently; no real secret is used.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given theme persistence accepts only the two selected literal values
When each controlled read, selection and storage-failure row is evaluated independently
Then stored invalid or missing values follow the system preference without unsafe interpretation
And a rejected selection changes no theme or stored value
And a valid selection updates memory even when persistence fails and no other key/store is used
```

**Verification:**

| Independent row | Initial input | Expected theme / storage observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stored dark | system light, stored `dark` | dark; read only spoolin.theme; no rewrite |
| Stored light | system dark, stored `light` | light; no rewrite |
| Missing | absent key with system dark, then light in a reset row | matching system theme; no new entry written without explicit valid selection |
| Invalid stored | each rejected exact value with system light/dark | system theme only; remove invalid spoolin.theme when permitted, no executable/style/selector value |
| Read unavailable | get throws; system light | light in memory; no new entry or unsafe storage fallback |
| Removal unavailable | invalid stored; remove throws | system theme remains usable; no new entry, and failure cannot select invalid value |
| Valid write | choose dark, then light in independent rows | requested value in memory; only setItem(spoolin.theme, exact allowed value) |
| Write unavailable | stored dark/current dark; choose light; set throws before change | light in memory remains usable; no alternative store/key |
| Invalid write | current light/stored dark; each invalid request | current light and stored dark unchanged; no write |
| Prototype alias | only movie-design-theme=dark; system light | light; prototype key is never read as a production alias |

Compare exact rule outputs and storage-call arguments with this hand-defined table; use no trimming, case folding, JSON coercion or prototype alias. The preference carries no actor/credential/draft data and cannot grant permission. This unit witness does not establish browser storage, rendered focus/theme behavior or session isolation; real complementary cases supply those boundaries.

**Complementary cases:** [ATDD-268](#case-atdd-268-one-theme-switch-preserves-the-same-interaction), [ATDD-336](#case-atdd-336-keep-protected-data-out-of-browser-persistence)

**Cleanup:** Discard only isolated rule inputs, storage spy and in-memory theme state.

[Catalog/theme](design-system/mockup/discovery.html#catalog), [expired](design-system/mockup/session.html#expired), [other account](design-system/mockup/session.html#other-account), [recheck](design-system/mockup/session.html#recheck), [review](design-system/mockup/ai.html#chatgpt). ```gherkin

```gherkin
Then application persistence writes explicit theme choices only as dark or light under spoolin.theme
And credentials, account projections, drafts even encrypted, challenges and API responses are never persisted in the forbidden stores, URLs, history payloads, telemetry or bundles
And allowed temporary form/CSRF state stays memory-bound and B cannot recover A state
And theme switching remains usable on storage failure without granting access or destroying eligible server-side draft recovery
```

**Verification:** Install observational hooks before actual application code loads and enumerate scoped localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/Cache API contents before, during and after every workflow. Preserve behavior when observing calls; a clean starting/final store alone or simple plaintext-canary search cannot prove absence of transient/encoded writes. Assert no application persistence writes except the exact validated theme key/value, no protected/API response persistence or alternate encrypted store, and no sensitive URLs/history state/log/bundle emission. Use actual APIs/owner rows to confirm authorized encrypted server draft persistence; reload/recovery queries current eligible server state and never invents a lost historical operation identity. Real rendered theme changes/reload use the valid value; invalid stored values are ignored/removed when possible (a removal-denied preexisting value may remain without being used), prototype key is not an alias and storage faults leave in-memory selection working. Inspect actual visible concealment/B-isolation and successful readable CSRF header submission from memory; do not require CSRF to be unreadable or absent from its declared JSON/anonymous cookie mechanism. The served review resource is checked for its own application-controlled storage calls; controlled host bridge inputs are labeled and cannot establish actual ChatGPT/Claude isolation, which remains separate real-client evidence. Browser-owned session restoration/password manager/files are not claimed to be controlled or absent.
