### Case ATDD-337: Enforce non-persistent secure session cookies

**Sources:** FR-011, NFR-008, NFR-015, AC-048, TD-SESSION, TD-CSRF, TD-PRIVACY, TD-SESSION-PERSISTENCE, TD-SESSION-COOKIE-LIFECYCLE, TD-SESSION-DELIVERY, TD-COOKIE-RESIDUAL, TD-CWE-539, TD-CWE-614, TD-ASVS-SESSION-CROSSWALK, TD-STORAGE-CHANNELS, TD-CSRF-READABLE, TD-COOKIE-NOALTERNATIVE, TD-COOKIE-LOGOUT, TD-COOKIE-RESTORE, TD-COOKIE-LOCAL, ASVS5-3.3.1, ASVS5-3.3.2, ASVS5-3.3.3, ASVS5-3.3.4, ASVS5-14.3.3, ASVS5-7.3.1, ASVS5-7.3.2, ASVS5-7.4.1, CWE539-CLASS, CWE614-CLASS, TD-BROWSER-RESPONSIBILITY

**Priority:** P0

**Level:** Integration

**Platform:** Real browser, HTTPS/Core, local MCP boundary

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Independently reset F-STACK/F-ACTORS and F-BROWSER-POLICY with actual production frontend, trusted HTTPS/Core and owner PostgreSQL. Use real browser APIs/events and scoped storage observations; controlled faults are explicitly labeled and do not prove host/provider behavior.

**Test data:** F-BROWSER-POLICY with A synthetic session, captured issuance/rotation/logout headers, eligible/restored/idle-expired/absolute-expired/auth_epoch-revoked rows, controlled lost reply and local listeners without connector credentials. Use F-EXPIRY exact cutoffs and separately recorded supported browser/profile restore settings.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given a synthetic account signs in through the actual trusted HTTPS/Core browser boundary
When issuance, actual renewal paths, rotation, confirmed and uncertain logout and browser restoration are exercised independently
Then authentication credentials are Set-Cookie-only and issuing or renewing cookies have the selected flags and no persistent lifetime attributes
And confirmed logout deletes the matching cookie with Max-Age=0 and invalidates its Core session
And restored cookies authenticate only while current server checks permit and expiry or revocation remains authoritative
And script-readable CSRF is distinct from the HttpOnly credential while other listeners accept no browser-cookie authentication
```

**Verification:**

| Independent transition | Header / real boundary oracle |
| --- | --- |
| Sign-in / rotation / any designated issuing path | __Host-spoolin_session; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; no Domain, Expires or Max-Age. Compare rotated credential privately; old fixed/replaced credential does not authenticate |
| Actual renewal or reissue | Inspect every path that actually emits the session cookie: same scope/flags, no Expires/Max-Age. A server last_seen refresh need not emit a new cookie; no extra renewal endpoint is invented |
| Confirmed logout | Core invalidates original session and emits matching deletion with Max-Age=0; browser removes cookie and old credential replay fails |
| Lost logout response | No confirmed-revocation claim from UI deletion alone; protected state locks and existing result/session lookup resolves outcome without retrieving raw credential from receipt |
| Valid browser restoration | A retained non-persistent cookie may remain valid; current Core verification/eligibility gates continuation rather than treating browser closure as revocation |
| Independently expired or revoked restoration | Still-present cookie fails Core eligibility at expiry/revocation, before purge; no private response/submission authority returns |
| Delivery / script visibility | Cookie value absent from JSON, URLs, receipts, diagnostics and application stores; document.cookie cannot read authentication credential. Declared readable CSRF remains functional |
| Local listener / credential scope | Inspect trusted configured HTTPS and Secure attribute; do not use localhost plaintext suppression or port differences as an oracle. A browser cookie alone cannot authenticate MCP/other listeners or enter their logs |

Capture every raw Set-Cookie line transiently through the privileged driver, parse attributes independently of framework helpers and retain only redacted name/attribute/status/rotation evidence. Inspect real browser cookie session classification and script visibility plus actual Core hashed rows/revocation/authorization; cookie deletion alone cannot prove server invalidation. Raw opaque value must never enter test logs, reports, HARs or persistent driver state as application data. Force before/at/after idle/absolute cutoffs through selected controlled owner fixtures; preserve five sessions/account, current epoch and sign-in rotation. Use actual browser close/restore capability with valid, expired and revoked controls; if restoration is unavailable record that unexercised branch rather than using a synthetic event as proof. Hostname/path scoping does not isolate localhost ports; exercise the actual MCP boundary with Cookie but no connector credential, observe denial and no raw-cookie diagnostic emission. Keep existing anonymous readable CSRF cookie and authenticated Session.csrfToken/header continuity valid. Non-persistent issuance is selected SpoolIn policy mapped to CWE-539, while missing Secure maps to CWE-614; no claim of disk absence, universal localhost transmission behavior or ASVS certification follows.

Static app assets and artwork form separate controls. A’s dirty non-secret permitted form, same-account recheck success, B switch, expiry/revocation, pending/unavailable verification and valid restored page are independently reset.

**Expected UI:** Shared shell and existing /manage/movies/[id] or /manage/people/[id] forms; [checking](design-system/mockup/session.html#session-check), [expired](design-system/mockup/session.html#expired), [recheck](design-system/mockup/session.html#recheck), [other account](design-system/mockup/session.html#other-account), [uncertain sign-out](design-system/mockup/session.html#signout-uncertain). Restored protected presentation starts concealed with submission unavailable while checks run. Denial/unavailability keeps it concealed and offers safe public navigation/sign-in; same-owner recovery is shown only after all existing checks. Current permitted focus/form values follow state-specific concealment/clearing rules, not blanket retention.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin

When GraphQL outcomes, pagehide/pageshow, history restoration and session/account transitions occur
Then every GraphQL response including errors has Cache-Control no-store while artwork and static assets retain their selected independent policies
And pagehide locks and detaches protected presentation before freeze and pageshow rechecks Core before unlocking

And only same-account current eligibility may resume allowed concealed memory or current server recovery without stale receipt or payload invention
```

**Verification:** Inspect the actual wire Cache-Control directives for all defined success/error paths, including pre-dispatch malformed/content-type/CSRF/origin/auth/429/413/503 and safe unexpected failures where their existing contracts apply; retain existing status/body mappings rather than invent a response code. A no-store directive must be present even on HTTP200 domain rejection. Observe network responses plus absence of persistent application response-cache writes; current authorized in-memory query state follows the existing invalidation/cleanup rules. Headers alone do not prove DOM cleanup or universal browser-profile erasure. Artwork remains no-store. Static HTML/CSS/JS retain their declared caching and usability; do not require disabling all caches or manufacture a service worker. Drive real navigation/pagehide/pageshow/history with Core responses held pending/unavailable and account A/B/expiry/revocation controls. Before freezing/restoring inspect actual visible DOM, accessible values, controller/handle cleanup and locked submissions; on return require completed current session checks before any reveal, followed by target/version/policy/original-operation checks for same-owner recovery. Record actual persisted pageshow/BFCache support when exercised; fresh navigation is a valid separate path, not proof that a frozen-page branch ran. Permitted non-secret values may remain only in the existing concealed account-bound RAM slot, never history.state/URL/persistent stores; that slot does not resist XSS, and escaping/CSP remain required. Browser closure does not revoke an eligible session, while expired/revoked restore cannot expose private data. Original Core intent absence after full reload gives no historical receipt/payload recovery promise.

### Case ATDD-339: Encode bounded private-safe JSON log records

**Sources:** TD-PRIVACY, TD-LOG-JSON, TD-LOG-PRIVACY, TD-LOG-SINK, TD-LOG-FIELD-level, TD-LOG-FIELD-timestamp, TD-LOG-FIELD-trace_id, TD-LOG-FIELD-span_id, TD-LOG-FIELD-message, TD-LOG-FIELD-resource, TD-LOG-FIELD-attributes, TD-LOG-FIELD-caller, TD-LOG-FIELD-dropped_attributes_count, TD-LOG-FRAMING, TD-LOG-EXCLUSIONS, TD-LOG-ENCODING, TD-LOG-REJECT-FIELDS, TD-LOG-ENCODED-BOUND, MEKARI-LOG-JSON, MEKARI-LOG-REQUIRED, MEKARI-LOG-ATTRIBUTES, MEKARI-LOG-PRIVACY

**Priority:** P0

**Level:** Unit

**Platform:** Log encoder and safe projection module

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Instantiate the isolated encoder/configuration/classification rule only, with controlled clock/context/resource inputs and a memory output spy. No runtime, database, network, provider, real logger sink or browser is started.

**Test data:** F-LOG controlled event time 2026-10-13T12:00:00.123456789Z, trace a1ac0334fcb72ad1513859d416b5ff26/span b819e2324b94eacd, Core/test/example-build resource and correlation UUID 8a30868c-2fbe-4093-aaab-e054c4a1a7c9. Each invalid field/byte/optional-attribute row starts from a complete valid record. Use synthetic private canaries and duplicate-key input pairs before map construction; malformed JSON strings are inputs, never emitted record templates.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given only approved operational fields may enter an application diagnostic record
When valid, malformed, duplicate, oversized and private-bearing inputs are independently projected and encoded
Then valid output is one complete LF-terminated UTF-8 JSON object with independently expected types and values
And invalid required data yields only a small fixed logger-contract error or count
And rejected optional fields and all private values cannot return through messages or dropped-value data
And encoding never produces a forged second physical line or truncates serialized JSON
```

**Verification:**

| Independent rule | Input | Expected observable output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid baseline | info; fixed Request completed summary; the named clock/context/resource | One compact object plus LF; decoded timestamp exactly 2026-10-13T12:00:00.123456789Z; trace/span/correlation preserved in separate fields; required resource has core/example-build/spoolin/test |
| UTC precision | Controlled UTC instants with0,3,6,9 available fractional digits; timezone-free or non-UTC timestamp is a separate invalid input | Valid UTC representation ends Z, preserving available precision/event time; invalid required timestamp produces safe contract error/count |
| Untraced boot | No active context | trace_id=32 zero characters and span_id=16 zero characters; no fabricated active span |
| Trace shape | Independently31/32/33 hex and15/16/17 hex, uppercase/nonhex, nonzero span with zero trace | Valid exact lowercase 32/16 only; invalid required tuple yields safe contract error/count. Boundary regeneration is tested separately in341 |
| Message byte bound | Fixed code summaries at255/256/257 UTF-8 bytes, including multibyte text | 255/256 retained unchanged;257 yields safe contract error/count, never truncated or echoed. User-supplied message text never replaces fixed summary |
| Resource | Omit required name/version/namespace/env; wrong type or unknown service/env; build version127/128/129 bytes | Complete selected resource only; valid 128 byte version preserved; invalid required resource yields safe contract error/count |
| Optional map | Allowlisted typed fields; string127/128/129 bytes; finite count/duration 0 and fractional duration; negative/NaN/infinity or wrong types | Valid bounded values preserved. Invalid optional fields omitted and safely counted; no array coercion, nonfinite JSON or private fallback. Lowercase, hyphenated UUID is validated independently |
| Optional keys/cap | Unknown key, repeated key/value pairs before map construction, >16 supplied fields | Unknown/excess fields omitted/countable; duplicate keys rejected before encoding rather than last-write-wins. Actual emitted attributes <=16; rejected values absent from all auxiliary fields |
| Private/exception input | Each F-PRIVACY category in nested attrs, raw exception message/cause/stack/entity/protocol object and user-shaped keys | Fixed safe summary/code/allowlisted error_class only; no auto serialization, private key/value, dropped_attributes list, SQL/body/header dump or raw exception text |
| Caller | Default absent; optional valid project-relative location; absolute workstation/user path | Default omitted; valid code-only location permitted; unsafe optional location omitted/countable without echoing path |
| Escaping | Fixed trusted code-summary fixture with CR/LF/quote/backslash/control characters; malicious input separately rejected | JSON serializer escapes characters; precisely one physical object/LF. Independent parser recovers the trusted fixture exactly; rejected hostile values never become a line/key |
| Encoded bound | Valid schema-sized records and synthetic oversized required/optional inputs at 16383/16384/16385 encoded bytes where representable | Every emitted record <= 16,384 bytes and parses completely; optional omission precedes encoding, invalid/oversized event becomes small safe contract error/count. No fabricated valid record is required if narrower field bounds make a target size unrepresentable |

Compare decoded keys/types/values and independently measured UTF-8 bytes against this hand-defined table, using a strict duplicate-aware parser independent of the encoder and no key-order requirement. Probe all synthetic private categories, not only a plaintext substring in final output: capture projection/serialization calls transiently and assert forbidden objects are never serialized. Retain only booleans/counts, never raw canaries. This proves isolated construction and failure classification; real framework bypasses, streaming, context lifetime and queue/storage durability require 341/342. Safe drop/counting is not a lossless diagnostic promise.

### Case ATDD-340: Select log severity and validate logging configuration

**Sources:** VERIFY-V-CONFIG, TD-LOG-LEVELS, TD-LOG-CONFIG, TD-LOG-FIELD-level, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-debug, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-info, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-warning, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-error, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-fatal, TD-LOG-MAPPING, TD-LOG-CONFIG-PRECEDENCE, CONFIG-Logging, MEKARI-LOG-LEVELS

**Priority:** P1

**Level:** Unit

**Platform:** Severity classification and configuration module

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Instantiate the isolated encoder/configuration/classification rule only, with controlled clock/context/resource inputs and a memory output spy. No runtime, database, network, provider, real logger sink or browser is started.

**Test data:** Controlled event kinds and framework TRACE/INFO/WARN/ERROR; LOG_LEVEL absent, info, debug, empty, whitespace, DEBUG, warning, error, false and unknown. Environment/file/default conflicts use explicit sources, with no live restart. Treat domain result/code as independent of HTTP200; provider delivery states come from selected owner truth.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given application levels describe the actual classified event and configuration permits info or debug
When event kinds, framework aliases, effective source precedence and invalid values are independently evaluated
Then expected validation and conflict are info while handled denial or degradation is warning
And failed work is error and unrecoverable startup is fatal without claiming the logger terminates the process
And omitted configuration is info, valid debug enables bounded detail, and invalid configuration blocks readiness
And both modes retain required outcomes and the same private-data exclusions
```

**Verification:**

| Independent row | Controlled input | Expected rule result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal lifecycle/domain | ready/start/completed, validation rejection, stale conflict, successful replay | info; correct fixed outcome/code; rejection cannot masquerade as success |
| Handled/degraded | CSRF denial, quota rejection, retry scheduled, uncertain external effect | warning; distinct denial/retry/uncertain outcome/code |
| System/security/integrity | dependency unavailable, exhausted work, encryption authentication failure, even HTTP200 | error; source-selected failed outcome/code, never info because HTTP status is200 |
| Unrecoverable prerequisite | invalid required key/config/schema | fatal classification; no simulated process termination claim; later command case proves failed exit/readiness |
| Optional detail | permitted execution/timing diagnostic | debug; no private payload in either mode |
| Framework mapping | TRACE, INFO, WARN, ERROR | debug, info, warning, error exactly; unrecoverable startup explicitly fatal; no emitted warn/TRACE/notice/critical/alert alias |
| Default | LOG_LEVEL absent in env/file | info; debug detail suppressed; required info/warning/error/fatal outcomes retained |
| Selected debug | Exact debug | permitted debug plus all required info/warning/error/fatal; unchanged redaction |
| Source precedence | env info/file debug; env debug/file info; env absent/file debug | info; debug; debug respectively. Default used only when both absent |
| Invalid effective input | empty/whitespace/DEBUG/warning/error/false/unknown; invalid env with valid file | Validation fails readiness with safe setting name/correction, no value echo/fallback. Invalid selected source is not treated as absent |
| Application timing | Validated info→debug→info revisions | Rule yields correct effective configuration per restart revision; isolated rule cannot prove live restart/hot-reload enforcement |
| Evidence meaning | APPROVED vs published; RECORDED vs provider accepted vs confirmed delivery | Preserve distinct fixed classifications/outcome values; logging never upgrades authority or delivery truth |

Use independently enumerated expected pairs, a memory emission spy and explicit event/result inputs; do not calculate expectations by calling the production classifier. Configuration validation and encoder success do not prove failed startup exits, cross-service readiness/restart, actual SLF4J/Node aliases, queue delivery or persisted audit.342 and218 supply those boundaries. No input mode may enable bodies/credentials/rawThrowable dumps, disable audit or claim same-origin/Cookie protection from logging alone.

Resolve exact instrumentation/build versions before execution. Named synthetic faults do not establish an external provider or chat-host guarantee.

```gherkin
Given each real ingress and worker attempt owns its execution context
When trusted calls, untrusted headers, concurrent cancellation and a worker restart are exercised independently
Then Core and MCP create trusted roots and internal mTLS child calls keep the trace with distinct child spans
And malformed or hostile context cannot choose actor, operation, receipt access or inherited private state

Inspect every start/completion/finally path: B must not inherit A's trace/span, correlation or account projection, and an untraced boot event alone may use zero IDs. On actual worker crash/restart, compare retained work/receipt/attempt evidence and original correlation UUID from fresh database readers; the resumed attempt emits a new trace and properly scoped spans without resetting generation/budget/effect identity. Use existing destination receipt/reconciliation cases for whether a send repeats; log counts alone cannot prove exactly-once effects.

User-facing error stays existing safe correlationId; no added public trace field or authentication source is inferred. Trace/UUID must not become metric labels or expose private receipt data. Retain each record's emitting service resource; outbound peer is separate. Test all info/debug modes and safe early/failed paths with F-PRIVACY absence, strict source codes and actual framework/context adapters. ### Case ATDD-342: Enforce JSON diagnostics and bounded sink failure behavior

**Sources:** D23, BRAIN-D23, VERIFY-V-CONFIG, VERIFY-V-OPS, CMD-make-logs, TD-PRIVACY, TD-LOG-JSON, TD-LOG-LEVELS, TD-LOG-CONFIG, TD-LOG-PRIVACY, TD-LOG-SINK, TD-LOG-FIELD-level, TD-LOG-FIELD-timestamp, TD-LOG-FIELD-trace_id, TD-LOG-FIELD-span_id, TD-LOG-FIELD-message, TD-LOG-FIELD-resource, TD-LOG-FIELD-attributes, TD-LOG-FIELD-caller, TD-LOG-FIELD-dropped_attributes_count, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-debug, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-info, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-warning, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-error, TD-LOG-SEVERITY-fatal, TD-LOG-FRAMING, TD-LOG-MAPPING, TD-LOG-CONFIG-PRECEDENCE, TD-LOG-EXCLUSIONS, TD-LOG-ENCODING, TD-LOG-REJECT-FIELDS, TD-LOG-ENCODED-BOUND, TD-LOG-QUEUE-BOUND, TD-LOG-FALLBACK, TD-LOG-AUDIT-INDEPENDENCE, TD-LOG-STREAMS, CONFIG-Logging, MEKARI-LOG-JSON, MEKARI-LOG-REQUIRED, MEKARI-LOG-LEVELS, MEKARI-LOG-ATTRIBUTES, MEKARI-LOG-PRIVACY

**Priority:** P0

**Level:** Integration

**Platform:** Actual application logger/framework, managed sinks, stdio MCP, private metrics and PostgreSQL

**Category:** Edge

**Automation:** Candidate

**Status:** Not Run

**Preconditions:** Reset F-STACK/F-ACTORS/F-LOG independently. Use actual selected JVM logger adapters, Node MCP/stdio bridge, trusted HTTPS, TCP mTLS owner services, PostgreSQL and private metrics. Resolve exact instrumentation/build versions before execution. Named synthetic faults do not establish an external provider or chat-host guarantee.

**Test data:** F-LOG independent boot/framework/ORM/ingress/worker records: ready, validation/conflict, CSRF/quota denial, dependency outage, retry/uncertain effect, recovery exhaustion and crypto authentication failure, including HTTP200 domain/system failures. Use actual info/debug restarts, invalid LOG_LEVEL, record boundaries16384bytes, queue occupancy1023/1024/1025,10MiB×5rotation; slow consumer, stopped reader, disk-full/permission and broken-pipe failures. Inject synthetic private values only in transient isolated capture and retain redacted results.

**Scenario:**

```gherkin
Given application diagnostics and durable business evidence have separate responsibilities
When real framework output, severity/configuration, stdout/stderr, rotation and log-sink failures are independently exercised
Then application-owned records remain bounded private-safe JSON with the selected field shapes and levels
And stdio MCP stdout remains protocol-only while diagnostics use stderr
And slow or failed sinks retain bounded queues and observable dropped counts without recursive or raw fallback
And committed receipts, work attempts and audit retain their source-defined truth independently of diagnostic delivery
```

**Verification:** Independently parse each physical application diagnostic line from actual JVM SLF4J/Logback, ORM/framework adapters and Node helpers, including boot before context and early failures. Assert one LF-terminated complete UTF-8 object, required fields/resources and exact info/warning/error/fatal mapping for the named event rows. Suppress plain Boot banners/ANSI/raw console/stacktrace/body/header/SQL parameter/RPC dumps in both modes. Unknown/private fields cannot escape through messages, causes, caller or dropped-value lists. Simulated encoder output cannot establish actual framework configuration.

Change only selected LOG_LEVEL through source precedence and validated restarts: default info suppresses optionaldebug; exact debug enables permitted detail and returning info suppresses it; required lifecycle/security warning/error/fatal events remain in both. Invalid selected values fail actual readiness/start with the documented command exit and safe correction, never silently falling back. Fatal logging alone is not the failure-exit oracle. Verify finite bounded attributes, fixed summaries/error_class, code/outcome and timestamp event time; userinput/Throwable canaries must be absent at intermediate/final captures and alternate streams. View decoded strings through the actual operator viewing path as escaped text, without executing markup; no production UI page is invented.

Drive an actual queue fill with a held sink at 1023/1024 and attempted 1025 records, inspect maximum occupancy and drop counter, then resume/close the consumer. Use existing request/worker total deadlines to observe terminal outcomes rather than sleep-only oracles; diagnostics cannot indefinitely block them. Oversized/invalid required records produce only safe contract error/count, optionalinvalid fields omit/count, all emitted lines <= 16,384 bytes with no partial serialized truncation. When disk/pipe fails, inspect the alternate diagnostic stream for the same JSON/redaction, no recursion/raw fallback, and the private exporter for increased dropped-record count despite absent logs. Do not require a lost record to reappear or exact record counts under failure.

Run stdio bridge initialization/calls and its actual logger-failure paths: stdout contains valid negotiated protocol messages exclusively, stderr safe diagnostics; service container application records have resource identity and no prefixes. Keep native PostgreSQL/monitoring/tunnel output and human command/status output separately scoped; do not rewrite their protocols to satisfy JSON. Observe real10MiB×5/service rotation and bounded make logs with218; framework log content remains operator-only.

For the same independently reset successful mutation/work claim/completion and rollback/crash points, disable/block/fail log delivery and query actual receipt/durable_work/operational_event/catalog_audit_event from fresh readers. Existing required commits/rollback/attempt phases, authorized audit projection and retention are unchanged: log start is not successful mutation, no log does not prove rollback, threshold/drop cannot suppress durable evidence. Confirmation/approval/publication and RECORDED/ACCEPTED/DELIVERY_CONFIRMED remain distinct. Disk/pipe losses are truthful best-effort diagnostic evidence; real database/worker cases retain their own independent proof.

**Complementary cases:** [ATDD-339](#case-atdd-339-encode-bounded-private-safe-json-log-records), [ATDD-340](#case-atdd-340-select-log-severity-and-validate-logging-configuration), [ATDD-341](#case-atdd-341-keep-trace-context-scoped-to-real-requests-and-recovery), [ATDD-218](#case-atdd-218-bound-useful-logs-without-exposing-secret-payloads), [ATDD-154](#case-atdd-154-commit-work-ownership-before-sending-effects), [ATDD-226](#case-atdd-226-enforce-restricted-activity-and-attempt-phase-storage), [ATDD-224](#case-atdd-224-enforce-catalog-business-audit-storage-and-private-event-separation), [ATDD-332](#case-atdd-332-roll-back-the-whole-draft-mutation-receipt-and-redacted-audit-boundary)

**Cleanup:** Apply C-RESET to this unique owner/browser/process namespace; restore sink/configuration and release fault barriers, close all spans/handles and delete only scoped diagnostic copies after retaining redacted results. Cleanup failure remains recorded.

Current approved request on 12October2026 authorizes these explicit reconciliations and the F-BENCHMARK protocol. The PRD owns product behavior; the adopted design system owns presentation; the techdoc owns engineering within those commitments. The other coordinated chat saved techdoc1.7 with the approved naming and audit corrections; this ATDD consumed its final validated source hash without editing the governing file. Ordinary expiry follows the selected hard cutoff; exact SQL and noncontractual setting names are not invented acceptance decisions.

Other preserved reconciliations: unknown-year imported discovery does not waive manual/MCP create year; years1..9999 and literal slash-preserving arrays override illustrative widgets; atomic approve/create does not merge approval evidence into creation proof; mockup page-memory drafts do not establish encrypted server recovery; stable unchanged pages do not promise a cross-page snapshot under live edits; timeout/cancel does not prove rollback; database recording default supersedes external-delivery-only notification interpretations. TV remains read-only while shared-person changes can affect displayed TV credits.

### Revision1.2 source reconciliation

The approved joint security revision changes only the specifications: target session cookie __Host-spoolin_session, configurable authoritative shared quotas, explicit injection enforcement, and durable Core save/discard receipts. It preserves existing source IDs, namespaces, audit projections and physical table designs. Read argument and physical-versus-owner validation expectations are corrected above. New negative and concurrency cases complement earlier locking/version/impact/audit/work/lease cases rather than weakening them. Security intent, static checks and actual runtime evidence remain separate. No global skill changes or application execution were performed.

### Browser weakness-to-control coverage

These are selected design/verification mappings, with all cases Not Run. [CWE-539](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/539.html) concerns sensitive persistent cookies; [CWE-614](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/614.html) concerns missing Secure. Theme-only localStorage is a separate minimization policy. Exact [ASVS 5.0.0 cookie](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v5.0.0/5.0/en/0x12-V3-Web-Frontend-Security.md), [client protection](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v5.0.0/5.0/en/0x23-V14-Data-Protection.md) and [session](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v5.0.0/5.0/en/0x16-V7-Session-Management.md) identifiers apply to the stated aspects; this is not a whole-standard certification. Historical v4.0.3-3.2.3 storage and -3.4.1 Secure references retain their original context in the techdoc and are not relabeled as v5 controls.

| Concern / exact version | Enforcing control and observable proof | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CWE-539; v5.0.0-14.3.3 | Selected non-persistent opaque cookie; no sensitive fields/refresh alternative, Core expiry/revocation on restore. ASVS permits a controlled session-token exception; omission of issuance/renewal lifetime attributes is SpoolIn’s stricter policy | ATDD-171, ATDD-336, ATDD-337 |
| CWE-614; v5.0.0-3.3.1 | Core Secure attribute and actual configured HTTPS, without localhost/plaintext or port-isolation assumptions | ATDD-337 |
| v5.0.0-3.3.2 / -3.3.3 / -3.3.4 | Lax purpose; __Host- scope; HttpOnly Set-Cookie-only credential delivery. Readable anti-forgery material remains functional | ATDD-172, ATDD-337 |
| v5.0.0-14.3.1 / -14.3.2 / -14.3.3 | Frontend locked cleanup/current revalidation, all GraphQL no-store and scoped absence of sensitive client persistence | ATDD-179, ATDD-336, ATDD-338 |
| v5.0.0-7.3.1 / -7.3.2 / -7.4.1 | Core 30-minute idle/12-hour absolute and invalidation; browser cookie presence/closure does not override server eligibility | ATDD-171, ATDD-337, ATDD-338 |

Only the selected crosswalk controls are inventoried from these primary-source chapters; unrelated ASVS controls are not silently introduced. Their retrieved snapshots/fingerprints distinguish source review from future runtime evidence. Cookie/CSRF/locality and browser-owned persistence residuals stay explicit in the [technical control crosswalk](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#853-cwe-and-asvs-verification-crosswalk).

### Logging source resolution and proof boundaries

The [selected contract](04-spoolin-techdoc.md#1221-json-log-contract) applies Mekari page 48735256814 v26's JSON/severity/context intent while making resource identity mandatory and applying SpoolIn's stricter privacy/bounds. The normative attributes map governs its inconsistent later illustrative array prose; optional dropped-value examples cannot override forbidden-payload rules. Framework WARN maps warning; only selected levels/configuration are allowed. Operational correlation remains UUID, distinct from trace_id; public error contracts and SQL/protobuf fields are preserved. Native infrastructure and human command streams retain their explicit scope. No template example proves receiver compliance or selects employer SDKs/paid tooling.

339/340 prove isolated field, severity and configuration rules; 341/342 prove actual context/logger/sink composition.218 retains its existing command exit/tail/follow contract with parsed complete-line verification.172 makes secondary-cookie purposes and current-generation CSRF handling observable, preserving deliberate readability and exact session eligibility. Related PRD/brainstorming/design documents remain governing inputs: their correlated-log/privacy and session-state commitments are compatible; prototype theme persistence is still only presentation evidence. No required new product decision is unresolved. Execution remains blocked until actual instrumentation/version, sinks, trusted HTTPS/browser and owned runtime evidence are available; those prerequisites do not imply a passed logging or security check.

## Evidence and maintenance

All new cases are Not Run. A described defect/failure injection is a prospective failure signal, never an observed failing TDD run. Supplied design reports remain separate from acceptance execution:

| Supplied report | Revision / expectation | Environment / execution date | Scope / freshness |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Design-system original review | Build/repository revision not supplied; current source report references PRDv2.4 | Local static Chromium fixture checks, 10October2026 | Reported582state/theme/width combinations and interaction checks; brand expectations changed11October, so prior branding applicability is stale without impact review. No backend/provider/client proof |
| Branding verification | Exact executing build revision not supplied; report records adopted11Octoberbrand and source checks | Local headless Chromium, 11October2026 | Reported40page/theme/width combinations plus targeted rechecks/navigation; did not rerun582state matrix. No current production case pass |
| Contrast artifact | Source solid token pairs, current byte fingerprint in register | Report records38pairs; exact measurement runtime/version not supplied | Static solid-pair reference only; arbitrary images/font/AT/runtime states require fresh evidence |

Later result evidence records case and table row, exact application commit/build/images/locks, ATDD expectation revision/source hashes, environment/browser/client/provider/key epoch identifiers without secrets, execution time and outcome. Passed/Failed fields require attributable Evidence, Revision, Environment and Executed at. A blocked actual execution records Blocker. On source/scenario/setup/oracle changes, retain the historical result as Stale until documented impact review or fresh execution establishes applicability. A complete future specification may be Ready for implementation while every case remains Not Run; this revision specifies the required outcomes; execution and release evidence remain prerequisites.
